references.text: God gives humanity dominion over all animals, birds, and fish—the same dominion confirmed after the flood with the promise that fear and dread will rest upon the animals.
Nearly identical wording: God places fear and dread (מוֹרַאֲכֶם וְחִתְּכֶם) for Israel over all nations, just as He placed it over all animals after the flood.
The psalm praises humanity's dominion over creation—over sheep and cattle, wild beasts, birds of the sky, and fish of the sea—in line with God's order established after the flood.
James confirms that all kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures are tamed by humans, reflecting God's promise of human dominion over the animals.
The Letter to the Hebrews quotes Psalm 8 and reflects on how everything has been placed under humanity's feet, in accordance with God's original and renewed mandate for dominion over creation.
Contrast between the fear given by humans over animals (Gen 9:2) and God's fear over all creation at judgment (Ezek 38:20).
Genesis 1:28 establishes the dominion that Genesis 9:2 confirms and modifies with fear after the flood.
Contrast: Animals are given into human hands (Gen 9:2), while humans are given to animals as punishment (Ezek 29:5).
Contrast between humanity's dominion over animals (Gen 9:2) and human corpses as food for animals (Jer 34:20).
Genesis 1:26 establishes the mandate that Genesis 9:2 confirms and reestablishes after the flood.
Direct allusion to the creation mandate (Gen 1:28/9:2) applied to an earthly king.
Contrast: Animals are given into human hands (Gen 9:2), yet are called to eat human corpses (Ezek 39:17).
Contrast: Humans are given to animals as food (Ezek 39:4) instead of ruling over them (Gen 9:2).
Contrast: Human corpses become food for animals (Deut 28:26) instead of humans ruling over them (Gen 9:2).
Contrast: Animals are called to eat (Isa 56:9) instead of being under human control (Gen 9:2).
Contrast: The dead become food for animals (Jer 16:4) instead of ruling over them (Gen 9:2).
